fields.why: B's evidence for summary ('20.2% and 20.1% was similar') is itself a period comparison, and every claim is comparative; still, overall caregiving prevalence and the Figure's state prevalence map are single-quantity estimates, so summary is defensible.

Table 1 sets the full age (7), race/ethnicity (8), education (4), income and employment distributions side by side for caregivers vs noncaregivers and tests each category; the brief says to record anything that looks groupwise and mark that it resolves to finer contrasts, which B did and A explicitly declined.
Follows groupwise_any: age, race/ethnicity and the SES components (education, income, employment) each have three or more levels in Table 1.

Each category is tested on its own (indicator × time logistic model, per the Table 1 note), with no omnibus test across the levels; strictly each level is contrasted with all other levels rather than with a reference level, which per-group vs referent only best approximates.

brief_issues: The groupwise assessment values have no option for 'each level vs all others' (one-vs-rest indicator tests); per-group vs referent only is the closest fit.
